letters.letter: I am applying for the Backend Developer Intern position because building reliable services is the part of software engineering I enjoy most. In my third-year course project I designed a REST API in Java with Spring Boot for a campus room-booking system: five entities, JPA repositories, validation, and a PostgreSQL schema I normalised myself. I wrote the SQL migrations by hand, added indexes after profiling slow queries, and cut the main search from 1.2 s to under 100 ms. Our team of four used Git with pull requests and code review, and I set up a Docker Compose file so everyone ran the same database locally. I also wrote JUnit tests for the service layer and reached 80% line coverage. I would like to learn how a production team handles deployments, monitoring and incidents, and I can contribute from the first week to tickets that involve Spring services or SQL.

Testing is where I have found my place in computing, and the QA Automation Intern role matches exactly what I have been practising. For a software testing course I built a Selenium WebDriver suite in Java for an open-source shop application: 46 test cases organised with the page-object pattern, data-driven from CSV files, and run with JUnit 5. I later rewrote the ten flakiest tests in Playwright and compared the two tools on stability and run time; the Playwright version ran in half the time with no intermittent failures over 30 runs. All of the work is in a public Git repository with a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the reports. I enjoy writing clear defect reports with exact steps and evidence, and I would bring that discipline to your team while learning how you test at scale.

I want to join you as a Data Analyst Intern because I like turning messy data into decisions people can act on. In a statistics project I cleaned two years of public transport ridership data with Python and pandas, handled missing values and duplicate records, and loaded the result into a SQL database. I wrote queries with window functions to compare weekday and weekend demand per line, and presented the findings to our class in a Power BI dashboard with three pages: trends, peak hours and stations with falling use. The dashboard led the student council to propose two new bus times, which the transport office accepted. I am comfortable explaining results to people without a technical background and I would value learning how your analysts validate data before it reaches management.

For the past two years I have worked part time at the university help desk, answering about forty student requests a week by phone, email and in person, in Arabic and English. I learned to listen first, confirm what the person really needs and follow up until the problem is closed. I keep a shared Excel tracker for the desk with pivot tables that show the most frequent request types; after I presented it, the team wrote three new FAQ pages and repeat requests fell by a quarter. In my communication course I led a group presentation on handling complaints, which received the highest mark in the section. I would like to bring this experience to your Customer Experience team and learn how a large company measures and improves customer satisfaction.

I am a computer science student with a strong interest in server-side development. Over the summer I volunteered to build a small inventory service for a local charity: Java 17, Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA and MySQL. The charity still uses it to track donated items across two warehouses. I designed the database tables, wrote the SQL reports the manager asked for, and documented the API so that another volunteer could build the front end. I keep all my projects in Git and I have started learning Docker to make deployment simpler for them. I know I still have a lot to learn about performance and security, which is why I want an internship where experienced engineers review my code.

My final-year project analyses electricity consumption in university buildings. I collect hourly meter readings, store them in a SQL database and use Python with pandas and matplotlib to detect unusual consumption at night. The model has already flagged two buildings where air conditioning ran over the weekend, and facilities fixed the schedules. I have taken courses in databases, statistics and data visualisation, and I am now teaching myself Power BI to share results with people who do not use Python. The Data Analyst Intern position would let me work with real business data and learn how analysts check the quality of their sources, which is the part of my project that took the most time and taught me the most.

I am interested in the Backend Developer Intern position at your company. I have studied Java in two programming courses and I used SQL in my database course, where we designed a library database and wrote queries. I have not used Spring yet but I have watched tutorials and I am confident I can learn it quickly. I am a hard worker and I work well in teams. I believe this internship will help me improve my skills and prepare for my career as a software developer. Thank you for considering my application.

I would like to learn more automation tools during the internship.
